terra.problem: The psalm does not say that David is not marching out with a sword.
The pan-of-dough comparison does not match the action: David asks that a trap set for him catch its makers.
The verse does not say that David will be out in the open after rescue.
The verse calls the people afflicted, poor and needy; it does not say they cannot help themselves.
The verse does not say that the people the LORD delivers cannot rescue themselves.
David says his prayers returned unanswered, but the text does not specify that he prayed for those people.
David says he grieved when they were ill, not that he grieved with them.
David compares his attackers to godless jesters at a feast. The explanation turns the comparison into a room full of mockers.
The explanation repeats that David said it without adding any insight. It sounds generic rather than like Papa Dorin.
David says he will give thanks in the assembly, but the text does not say he has no plan to thank the LORD quietly as well.
Calling the cave of Adullam a place from David's life brings in a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The text does not identify what the enemies claim to have seen, so it cannot say they saw David fall.
The last two sentences repeat the same point without adding anything. The explanation feels flat and generic.
The explanation repeats the answer in several ways without adding insight or Papa Dorin's personality.
The verse does not explicitly identify the servant as David, so the explanation should leave that identification open.
David does give a duration: all day long. Saying he puts no end date on it goes beyond the verse.
